content:
| Field | Example | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Place | Harbor steps | Human-readable label |
| Theme | welcome | Broad pattern for browsing |
| Evidence | observation | Distinguishes direct notes from interpretation |
| Consent | public summary | Controls what can leave the private library |
| Confidence | emerging | Keeps uncertainty visible |

These fields define the Atlas's working data model. The vocabulary reflects
the tradeoffs in [Design principles](/note/notes/design_principles) and should change
as the [research plan](/note/projects/neighborhood_atlas/research_plan) produces better questions.

occurrences.context: Noah applies these ideas to the Atlas data dictionary, especially the consent and evidence fields.
Start with the research plan and end by updating the data dictionary.
The data dictionary keeps those distinctions visible.
